name: Zephyr-Cairn
description: Zephyr-Cairn is a barren world where the faintest of breezes, barely perceptible in the thin atmosphere, has spent billions of years slowly stacking loose stones into natural cairn formations across the surface. These balanced stone columns, some reaching improbable heights in the low gravity, give the landscape the appearance of a vast, abandoned cemetery. Impact craters of various ages interrupt the cairn fields, their ejecta providing fresh material for the wind's patient construction.

The zephyr winds are so gentle that they cannot be felt on exposed skin, yet their effects are visible everywhere. Stones perch in precarious balance, held in place by forces barely stronger than the static charge between their surfaces. Walking through the cairn fields requires care, as disturbing even one stone can trigger a cascade that topples formations that took millions of years to build. The silence is near-absolute, broken only by the rare, soft click of a stone settling into place.

Among the natural cairns, a series of monolithic structures stands in an arrangement that matches no random distribution. These monoliths are composed of local stone but shaped with a precision that the zephyr winds could not achieve, their surfaces polished smooth and inscribed with geometric patterns. A low-power signal emanates from the largest monolith, detectable only at close range, broadcasting what appears to be a stellar map that includes several systems not catalogued in any current database.

Zephyr-Cairn's monoliths and their stellar map have drawn the attention of deep-space exploration advocates who believe the map indicates destinations worth reaching. The uncatalogued systems are beyond current survey range, making verification impossible without significant investment in long-range probes. The planet itself has little to offer beyond the mystery, its minerals unremarkable and its environment merely inhospitable rather than dangerous. Yet the possibility that the monoliths are a signpost, left by unknown hands for unknown travelers, keeps Zephyr-Cairn on the charts.
